transcript:
This is NPR News now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Korova Coleman.
President Trump has landed in the Philippines' capital Manila for high-level meetings.
He's arrived in time for dinner with other leaders attending the ASEAN summit.
Russia and Ukraine targeted each other's bridges overnight in missile attacks.
NPR's Eleanor Beersley reports explosions rocked Ukraine's capital Kiev as key bridges
linking the city's left and right banks were targeted.
NPR reporters witnessed multiple explosions as Kiev's northern and southern bridges over
the Nipro River were targeted by ballistic missiles after midnight.
Kiev Mayor Vitaly Klitschko filmed himself on one of the damaged bridges where it looks
like cables on one side have snapped.
President Volodymyr Zelensky warned that Russia is trying to divide Ukraine in half along
the Nipro River.
Kiev would be paralyzed if its two banks were cut off from each other.
Ukraine overnight attacked Russia's Kerch bridge with its Flamingo missiles.
The Kerch bridge links Russia's mainland with the occupied Crimean Peninsula.
Pictures posted to social media show one of the structure's arches and roadway between
two supports completely gone with debris below.
Eleanor Beersley, NPR News, Kiev.
The Pentagon confirms a third U.S. aircraft carrier has arrived in the mid-east.
NPR's Quill Lawrence has mourned.
U.S. Central Command posted on social media that the USS Theodore Roosevelt Carrier Strike
Group has arrived in the Middle East as part of what it calls a scheduled deployment.
The build-up of American firepower is a contrast to recent comments by President Trump that
the war is effectively over.
Major combat operations stopped during the summer, leaving a stalemate.
The U.S. continues to blockade Iranian ports, and Iran still controls the Strait of Hormuz,
which has driven up prices of petroleum products worldwide.
Iran is likely to be a topic when President Trump meets with the leaders of China and
Russia this week.
Russia's Vladimir Putin has openly supported Iran in the conflict.
Quill Lawrence, NPR News.
United Airlines says a system glitch is to blame for yesterday's 90-minute outage yesterday
delaying some flights.
This comes on top of last Friday's massive ground stoppage that delayed all departing
flights nationwide for hours.
Investigators are analyzing the router that likely caused that ground stop.
But Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy is seeking more funding from lawmakers to pay
for upgrades.
And Piers Jo Hernandez says Congress may not be so quick to agree.
Congress appropriated $12.5 billion last year for an upgrade to the air traffic control
system.
This week, Secretary Duffy asked Congress for another $30 billion, and then later said
what he really needed was $50 billion.
So Democrats have balked at those numbers.
They say the FAA still hasn't spent all of the initial $12.5 billion it got.
NPR's Jo Hernandez prepared that report.
You're listening to NPR.
The Pan American Health Organization is scheduled to announce whether measles has again become
endemic in the United States.
Scientists believe the answer is yes.
The organization will determine whether the U.S. will lose its official designation as
a country that has eliminated measles.
Vaccination rates in the U.S. have fallen, and more than 5,200 cases and eight deaths
have been reported by states.
The late civil rights and labor leader Dolores Huerta made history this week.
She became the first woman and first non-elected person to lie in honor at the California State
Capitol in Sacramento.
From member station KQED, Farida Jabela Romero has more.
Hundreds of people, including the first Latino governor-elect in California's modern history,
walked in a procession behind a hearse carrying Huerta's casket to the Capitol Building in
Sacramento, many chanting "Yes, we can."
Sarah Almaraz drove three hours from the city of Fresno with her 10-year-old son to pay
her respects.
Definitely an historic moment for all of us in California, especially Latinos.
I think that what she's done has given people just the realization that everyday people have
power.
Huerta, who co-founded what became the United Farm Workers, died of cancer last month at
age 96 in Bakersfield.
For NPR News, I'm Farida Jabela Romero in Sacramento, California.
And I'm Corva Coleman, NPR News from Washington.

topics.text: President Trump lands in Manila for ASEAN summit meetings and dinner with leaders
Russia and Ukraine strike each other's bridges overnight, with explosions reported in Kyiv
Pentagon confirms third U.S. aircraft carrier, USS Theodore Roosevelt, arrives in the Middle East
United Airlines blames system glitch for 90-minute outage delaying some flights
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy seeks $50 billion from Congress for air traffic control upgrades
Pan American Health Organization to decide whether measles has again become endemic in the U.S.
Dolores Huerta becomes first woman and first non-elected person to lie in honor at California Capitol
